item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hi there, I'm Luggy.
I haven't posted on here in years so I thought I may as well re-introduce myself.

I discovered SCP a long time ago through the numerous fan-games that it spawned. Back then, I joined the site to improve my English and try to write for the site. However, I was also a teen who had no idea of what he was doing, so that didn't go very far. It's only recently that I rediscovered the site thanks to channels like TheVolgun and The Exploring Series and it has renewed my love for the site.

Writing an SCP when you're 17 sounds great, but now that I'm older, my goals have changed. I just want to hang out here and maybe improve my writing while I'm at it. If you guys got any suggestions regarding the latter, I'd love to hear them.

As far as hobbies go, my main hobby is drawing. I'm not great at it, but it's still something I'm passionate about. You can check out my art on Newgrounds.
Despite being an English major (in France), I still need to read more. Forcing people to read books you don't care about does that to you.

What kind of random thoughts keep me up at night ? Most likely all my old posts on here that have been buried by time. Crazy how a person can change in a few years.

Hoping I'll hang out longer here. Cheers !

item.title: Re: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Porting PM conversation:

+ show block
– hide block

I do have an alternate idea involving an amber mist that transports beings to an oceanic "gateway" world. There, I was thinking of exploring an SCP agent interacting with a cetacean and insectoid, both of whom were also transported to the world. It'd be more of an exploration of power dynamics and territorial advantage between sapient species. Do you think that'd have a better chance than this?

It depends. Some reviewers might ask why you're not writing a tale instead, especially if the core anomaly is material that exists in various forms on the site already.

Largely because the SCP in question does lead to a unique world, which requires its own SCP article. Plus, the SCP itself has some unique properties beyond just transporting a person to another place. I was thinking it could also be fairly nutritious, which is a key reason why the SCP agent in the story I plan to tell doesn't die of scurvy or malnutrition after being at sea for so long.

If it's meant to be primordial, it seems odd that the seaweed would be so conveniently well adapted to a modern human's digestive system. I feel like a different narrative approach would be needed. Timespace oddities and whatnot might even make more sense here from a story standpoint.

Hm. The question is how to do that inside of four hundred words. Would it help if I mentioned it was meant to be in journal format? I know that's been done several times, but… looking over the SCP's, some of my favorite stories have been journal-like narratives, and I think it'd work well in this case.

Could you elaborate a bit? Like, suggesting that this takes place in a past era of Earth? Or that time moves differently in this world, and hunger becomes a non-issue? If it's the latter, I did have an idea about time moving differently on this alien world, so that could inform him returning and noticing that little time has passed.

For the new discussion, I feel like the core narrative needs to be better established before you start thinking about mechanics. What is the backstory behind the world's existence and why are random trespassers not immediately ejected? If we know why the world behaves the way it does, we can better advise on how to make the mist effect match.

item.title: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Basically a brainstorming thread for a potential SCP.

The idea behind it involves an SCP that, in its present state at the time of the article, is a tank of amber-colored water. In a solid or liquid state, the water has no special properties other than its unusual color. In a gaseous state, however - particularly a semi-gaseous mist - the water transports whomever travels through it to an oceanic world with no fauna.

Despite this, I'm thinking that the world is very friendly to life - the seas are freshwater, and there's a diverse ecosystem of plant life beneath the surface, some of which are edible and moderately nutritious to humans, despite their alien nature.

The SCP story itself involves an SCP scientist who's sent to investigate the unusual amber cloud hovering about a mile off the coast of Tanzania, when a powerful wind blows it into him before he has time to adjust his course, transporting him to the oceanic world, where he encounters a large sentient cetacean-like creature and a sentient, flying arachnid-like creature. The story itself would explore the backstory of the world, and the interactions of three sentient creatures and how they interact with their environment when they're unequally built for it, and the power dynamic that emerges as a result of their unequal adaptations.

I'm still figuring out the mechanics behind the mist itself, though the fact that it only facilitates transportation as a mist and not in any other state of matter is key to the story's resolution.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Dr Eden Knightly! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's awesome to see that you also think the SCP Wiki is an interesting place - hopefully, during your stay here, you're not going to get disappointed with all of the stories you'll get to read here. It's also really nice to see you want to contribute to that, too. I can't wait to see what you'll come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

I think I misinterpreted this idea a little. On a second read, it's not that similar to the other SCP, but I still find the "needing to sacrifice humans to feed the entity" part a bit too generic. Also, what's preventing the Foundation from just killing the girl? Will the entity latch on to someone else? I think this needs a bit more detail.

If I had to make a suggestion, I think this would be more interesting if the entity was making the girl sick but killing everyone who tried to separate it from her. You could even add in a more sympathetic angle for the entity - maybe it really doesn't want to hurt the girl or anyone else, but it just naturally causes death? Something of that type would interest me more.

item.title: SCP Greenlight Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror-ish

Elevator Pitch: A creature, which in dormant form heavily resembles a metal dog crate. It takes that shape in order to lure animals (and potentially people) inside, where it will commence torture and feed on their pain.

Central Narrative: After a gruesome, high-profile pet dismemberment, the SCP Foundation investigates the scene. They confiscate the crate in which the remains were found, and subsequent testing reveals it is in fact anomalous. At first, it is believed that the crate only moves when no one is looking at it, but testing reveals it's sentient and moves when it thinks no one is watching. Its hunting morph is a four-legged creature bearing a passing resemblance to a bear. When a biological creature enters the crate in dormant mode, the door will close and lock, and the wires of the cage will pierce its prey in deliberately non-lethal areas, in order to keep it alive as long as possible. After feeding on its victim's pains, it will typically enter its hunting morph, tear up the body into tiny shreds in an attempt to hide the evidence, and look for a new area to lie in wait.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A non-biological predator that preys on pain, hunts and kills sweet family pets, and has developed a merciless camouflage system.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: 432.7 Hz
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A Tone that is estimated to emit a frequency of about 432.7 Hz. The sound is immune to any sort of muffling via cognitive or physical means, and maintains an equal volume across a roughly 5 meter radius.

Central Narrative: A few research notes about the different properties of the sound, as it is both mobile and often hard to contain. The Foundation has decided to organize gatherings that create a large amount of noise in order to maintain containment, such as construction work or festivals. AWCY also plays a small part in this, as they occasionally try to create street music around the "sound".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A sound that follows none of the conventional laws of sonic physics, and is only perceptible by humans which creates some mystery around what it is.

Additional Notes: Deciding the class I feel might be a bit hard, as I feel like it may be Keter due to its generally hard to contain nature, however it could be Euclid I suppose too

item.title: Re: The Interdimensional Bodega
item.content:encoded:
Placeholder comment, will add in crit in a bit. So far, I like the concept of a non-violent resolution!

Edit:
Line-by-Line:

+ Show
- Hide

SCP-XXXX-1 is to be stationed with a concierge staffed by a Foundation personnel at all times.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but a concierge is a person, so it should be something like "SCP-XXXX-1 is to be staffed at all times by Foundation personnel, with at least one taking on the role of a concierge."

All entrants to SCP-XXXX-1 will allowed one of four choices:

This doesn't have the best clinical tone, I'd phrase it as "Upon entry, all entrants to SCP-XXXX-1 will be presented with a choice of four objects:"

The use of amnestics on entrants is punishable by termination.

Crank that way down. Termination means getting killed, usually, and the effects of amnesticization don't seem deserving of punishment via death.

SCP-XXXX is a symbol visible only to approximately 20% of the population. The reason for this is unknown.

First, scratch that entire second line. It's an anomaly, of course it's unknown. As for the first sentence, it moves too fast and doesn't give enough information. A symbol? What kind? Visible or invisible in what ways?

SCP-XXXX’s location varies, however, the most consistent location on which it is found is any type of featureless wall with high amounts of activity and traffic.

So it moves around? Or is someone drawing it in various places? You gotta explain things more.

Individuals who can see SCP-XXXX are granted access to SCP-XXXX-1; access to SCP-XXXX-1 is done by placing an open hand on SCP-XXXX. The wall on which SCP-XXXX is visible will then dissipate, revealing an entrance to SCP-XXXX-1.

Again, slow down the pacing. It's hard to understand what you mean here, even though you've given enough information.

Clothing themed after the GoI, the Wandsmen.

Hit the brakes. You're introducing an entire new GoI that we know nothing about in a single bullet point, and treating it casually like we're supposed to know everything about them. Also, you'd probably want to state it like "GoI-12345 'The Wandsmen'" or something more clinical.

How they obtained this information

"How this information was obtained"

SCP-XXXX-1’s main retail lobby is managed by PoI-XXXX (need better name later lol) and PoI-XXXX-2, bipedal avian creatures with features similar to owls (Strigiformes) and both standing at approximately 2 meters.

At this point, these two wouldn't be PoIs. They'd be subanomalies, like SCP-XXXX-2A and SCP-XXXX-2B.

- Hide

I'll admit I stopped reading at this point. You very consistently don't give enough information and are lacking clinical tone, to the point where the reader loses interest before they get to the logs. You move along far too quickly to set up any points of reference for the reader, which leads to me being halfway down the article and still feeling lost and confused.

Work on those things, then feel free to message me again to review the full draft.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Plastic Army
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout: The page will have the basic SCP article layout, but with addendums sharing the development of the army’s story.

Elevator Pitch: A collection of living Gundam models. Have organs underneath the plastic armor plates, but they do not match any living species. The models speak in the memories of American soldiers in the Vietnam War that seem to be from another timeline.

Central Narrative: Tells the story of American soldiers in the Vietnam War. The models were found in a former Vietnamese battlefield with significant damage. On the surface, there is nothing particularly strange about them. However, there appear to be functioning organs beneath the plastic armor plates that do not match up to any known species. Although they appear to be human-like, they contain DNA that varies greatly from those of humans. The living parts of all of the models are of the same species. The models cannot move, but they are known to speak. It speaks from the perspective of several soldiers such as General Richard Hall from the dates of November 8, 1955, to May 9, 1961. It begins with Richard Hall getting drafted, and later the other soldiers are seen getting drafted. The story from here on out consists mostly dialogue between the models, shouting during battles, and various promotions. At any points in time where a bodily fluid would be excreted by one of the soldiers, the model excretes the same fluid. Recorded excretions include blood, sweat, tears, and urine. Although the story encompasses almost seven years, the full seven years are not played out. Only select days are played out. These days include battles, significant interactions, and promotions. The full day is always played out. On the final day, there is a battle that all of the soldiers take part in. In this battle, they each comment on a creature that looks somewhat like a dog before dying. Upon death, they bleed profusely for 5 minutes before the organs cease function. After 214 hours, the story begins again the exact same way, in a cyclical nature. The real versions of these soldiers all had different positions. They all died on July 24, 2006.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Emotional story told by Gundams.

Additional Notes: I just really want this to be its best, since I'm not a super experienced writer.

1: There are a number ob SCP entries where the Foundation has advanced technology, sometimes even FTL capable vessels. So I think having a ship capable of travelling the solar system is normal for the Foundation.

2: I have not said it in the idea but I would set the SCP in a rather close orbit around the sun, thus it is very unlikely that anyone besides the Foundation / Foundation assets in gov space programs would find the SCP.

3: Well, the behavour of 106 is different, since it's main thing is to corrode things and pull people into another dimension. This SCP would leave structures intact, only attack within atmosphere and pulls people (partially) inside the walls but otherwise leaving them in our world. I will adjust the OP a bit to make that more clear.

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX "The Nightmare Victim"
item.content:encoded:
What you have here is still the basic of the basic and I doubt you'll get much attention to your article as it is now. This is basically a cursed object story and those have been made dozens of times at the SCP wiki and media in general. So far this proposal lacks a narrative arc that will get readers invested. Who is this Vivian Fay? Who killed her and why? Why has she become an anomaly when thousands of people are killed daily and most of them don't become anything? How did the Foundation got the knife?
Also, the whole naked woman covered in blood is… kinda old and tacky? Is there a reason for her to be naked and specifically have blood covering her intimate parts? If there isn't any reason for this I suggest scrapping this part and giving her a time appropriate outfit or just skip this description at all.

item.title: Re: Impregnating Ultrasound (Tale)
item.content:encoded:
I hammered mostly down on all the SPaG stuff and thought I should come back and give some more thorough thoughts on the actual story and pacing.

[+] Open
[-] Close

I already talked enough about the falling action of the Gregory-baby climax, but the rising action into it is also a bit lacking I feel. The rising action where Gregory gets snatched initially I feel you did nicely and it flowed pretty well, but the next one came out of left field completely, there was barely any indication that anything like this was going to happen. Suffice to say, I was not sufficiently mentally prepared for a tiny, middle aged man to come crawling out of a vaginal cavity. I was especially unprepared because of the similarity of this situation to the initial Gregory one where Gregory just simply disappeared and there were no established insane horror elements as of that point.

The introduction to Lisa's plan is perfectly fine, but it came off to me as a bit fast where she comes up with it and then executes it, she doesn't toil over whether or not she should do it before becoming strong in her conviction or whatever. But I would like to compliment you on revealing where the ultra sound machine was moved to, because when it is written that she asks the staff, you don't reveal where it actually is until James and Lisa are there doing the impregnating thing and I really liked that.

In the initial Gregory scenario, where he goes missing, I didn't immediately realize that he had literally disappeared in front of the lady who later birthed him. Consider, after it says Gregory wasn't in the room, mentioning that he hadn't left the room or have the lady remark that he vanished before her eyes.

A lovely day to you as well.

item.title: Re: A tale about the foundation’s attempts to deal with spies within the foundation
item.content:encoded:
Something like this lives and dies on a few things.

  1. Believable and relatable characters. They need good motivation of why they do what they do. They can't just be spies for the sake of it, since it will just look like a contrived ''Among us'' game with a Foundation theme. What do they want? Who are they? What are their strengths? What is their weakness? Personality traits? Do they develop relationships with Foundation personnel?
  2. The Foundation is one of the most clandestine and thoroughly professional organisations there is. You'd need a good, plausible reason for the Foundation to refrain from finding out that these people work for someone else. Every single one. You can't just bullshit your way into a Foundation Site with a fake ID and a winning smile.
  3. Just the hunt for spies is not enough. How do they find out there are spies without knowing who it is? What are the spies working towards? Are they working against each other?

These three things are going to be one of the major challenges, and I recommend getting those sorted out before even asking for greenlights, since you'd set yourself up for failure if you don't think these through beforehand.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: The Earworm
item.content:encoded:
Who doesn't like a good pun? The name alone just made me interested, I have a few concerns though.
The songs that activate the worms were specifically created with this purpose or it's just a coincidence? If it is on purpose, who is doing it? Considering that the affected individuals end up with reduced mental capacity it would be unlikely that one of them is responsible for the songs. I suggest changing the effect of the worm on the host and instead of making them feral making them more and more proficient at songwriting and composing, this way they could work on creating more songs to activate their eggs. You could even imply that many celebrities known for their popular appeal are, in fact, hosts of earworms working to increase their numbers. This is a funny but subtly terrifying concept and I hope you manage to get it into a full article.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "The Nightmare Victim"
item.content:encoded:
A bloodied, nude woman (don't worry, the blood covers anything inappropriate) that appears in the nightmares of her victims.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX appears to be a bloody, nude female entity (blood covers any extremities) with multiple stab wounds that appears in the nightmares of distinct individuals. Nearly all subjects reported seeing copious amounts of blood pouring out of said wounds.

All relevant data has been collected by interviewing test subjects (D-Class) directly exposed to SCP-XXXX-1, a handcrafted knife from the 14th century, after multiple sleep studies.

Central Narrative

+ show block
– hide block

90% of encounters follow this path; The subject walks into a dark room with bloody tools and knives lining the walls. In the center of the room is a table on which SCP-XXXX lies. Upon approaching the table, 100% of subjects reported that the figure began to rise from of the table and approach them.

SCP-XXXX-1 seems to have a strong connection to SCP-XXXX, possibly the weapon that killed it in the first place. The weapon had traces of blood in which the DNA of a young woman named "Vivian Fay" was extracted.

Hook/Attention Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

Contact with SCP-XXXX has been reported to cause several health issues, such as heart palpitations, unprovoked panic attacks and restricted airways, even in young, healthy individuals with no pre-existing conditions. In extreme cases it causes cerebral hemorrhaging and unexplainable chest wounds.
